footer.blurb:
Orbs is a “Layer-3” public blockchain infrastructure project powered by PoS, pioneering on-chain innovation since 2017.

Orbs is set up as a separate execution layer between L1/L2 solutions and the application layer, as part of a tiered blockchain stack, enhancing the capabilities of smart contracts and powering protocols such as dLIMIT, dTWAP and Liquidity Hub.

hero.headline:
TIME-WEIGHTED AVERAGE
PRICE PROTOCOL FOR
DECENTRALIZED EXCHANGES
hero.intro: Extend existing on-chain DEX/AMMs with a decentralized on-chain protocol for executing advanced time-spread algorithmic trades. Reduce large orders’ impact on the market.

benefits.title: The two benefits of TWAP
benefits.intro: **TWAP (Time-Weighted Average Price)** is an algorithmic trading strategy that divides an order into multiple smaller trades that are executed at regular intervals over a specified period of time.

priceImpact.title: Price Impact Reduction
priceImpact.body:
When a trade is relatively large or involves a low-liquidity pair, price impact will be high and cause significant losses to traders.

TWAP eliminates price impact by spreading the trade over several minutes. This gives arbitrageurs a time window to close price discrepancies and bring the reserves back to the fair market spot price.

dca.title: Automation of Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA)
dca.body:
DCA is an investing strategy that purchases an asset on a recurring long-term schedule (ie. on every Monday). 

The goal behind DCA is to average out abnormal market conditions and lessen the impact of short-term volatility on the overall purchase. A TWAP strategy can fully automate the DCA process.

schema.title: Decentralized Execution of TWAP Orders
schema.body:
**Makers** - The first entity in the dTWAP protocol are DEX traders that submit new orders to the dTWAP EVM contract. They set all order parameters such as limit price and expiration. The dTWAP contract enforces these requirements in a trustless manner.

**Takers** - Incentivized third-party participants that monitor all live orders and submit bids on the best path to execute their next segment. The dTWAP contract selects the best bid and guarantees that the path that provides the best price to makers is the one executed.

Orbs Network has dozens of independent validators running Proof-of-Stake consensus with over $100 million staked. The network has been running in mainnet since 2019. All Orbs Network validators are takers and participate as honest bidders in the protocol, guaranteeing that orders are executed 24/7 with high redundancy and best price.

Decentralized limit orders are not trivial to implement using smart contracts. Flawed implementation of limit orders in DeFi can hurt users by executing the order at a price much worse than they intended, or the order not being executed at all.

The dLIMIT smart contract for DEXs ensures that limit orders are executed at an optimal price and at fair fees, in a decentralized and reliable manner.

hero.headline:

decentralized exchanges
hero.intro: Liquidity Hub is a decentralized optimization layer that operates above Automated Market Makers (AMMs). This layer mitigates the problem of fragmented liquidity in DeFi, enabling DEXs to tap into external liquidity sources in order to provide better prices on swaps.

sources.intro: Instead of the typical swap that searches for the best route within a specific DEX's limited liquidity pools, integrating the Liquidity Hub software protocol allows DEXs to enhance this process by utilizing additional liquidity sources that come from:

solverAuctions.title: On-chain solver auctions
solverAuctions.body: Third-party solvers who compete to fill swaps using on-chain liquidity like AMM pools or their own private inventory.

apiOrders.title: Decentralized Orders via API
apiOrders.body: Decentralized limit orders, accessible using API. Enables institutional/professional traders, such as market makers, to submit bids and compete to fill swaps.

fallback.body: Utilizing the Liquidity Hub software allows DEXs to attempt to execute trades without going through the AMM and experiencing AMM price impact. If Liquidity Hub is unable to execute the trade at a better price than the AMM, the trade will fallback to the AMM contract and execute as usual.
fallback.alt: A swap routed through Liquidity Hub, comparing solver and API order sources against the AMM and falling back to the AMM contract when it cannot beat that price.

benefits.title: Integrate now with a user-friendly and flexible UI

lpCannibalization.title: Avoiding LP cannibalization
lpCannibalization.body: Existing DEX LPs generate the same revenue with Liquidity Hub enabled as they would have without it.

mevProtection.title: MEV protection
mevProtection.body: Arbitrage loss to MEV can be significant. Since Liquidity Hub matches orders without block producers, it removes MEV losses completely.

composable.title: Fully composable solution for Solvers
composable.body: Liquidity Hub supports UniSwapX and other similar protocols solver API, enabling anyone to participate in the bidding process right out of the box.

ceFiMarketMakers.title: Fully supports CeFi market makers
ceFiMarketMakers.body: Liquidity Hub protocol will allow DEXs to include a standard CEX book API allowing traditional MMs to participate in DeFi.

gasless.title: Gasless transactions
gasless.body: Liquidity Hub trades are **gasless** for users (although solvers may price gas into their fees).

decentralization.title: Mitigating Centralization risks using Orbs L3
decentralization.body:
All on-chain parts are trustless since contracts verify all actions. However, users may be concerned that Liquidity Hub backend is able to manipulate trades in some way. This concern is mitigated by using the Orbs Network's decentralized L3 technology.

As part of Liquidity Hub, Orbs Guardians will run software utilizing ORBS-VM, which acts as a decentralized backend that is required for Liquidity Hub to run optimally and in a fully decentralized manner.

The Orbs Network has dozens of independent validators running Proof-of-Stake consensus with over $100 million staked. The network has been running in mainnet since 2019.

The Liquidity Hub is a beta version that is still under active development.

hero.headline: Orbs Agentic
hero.intro:
The execution layer between AI agents and DeFi protocols.

When an agent needs to swap, place a limit order, or run a TWAP strategy, it calls an Orbs Agentic tool. The Orbs Network handles execution, routing, and cosigned-oracle verification — so every trade is independently verified on-chain.

Not a wallet. Not a custodial layer. Not AI trading. The verification layer that lets agents execute DeFi safely.

breaks.intro: The bottleneck holding back autonomous DeFi isn't reasoning. It's trust, safety, and execution.

safety.title: Safety
safety.body: Every trade is cosigned by an independent oracle before execution — agents can't go rogue.

quality.title: Execution quality
quality.body: Smart routing across DEXs with slippage protection, the same engine behind $2.2B+ in executed volume since 2022.

reliability.title: Reliability
reliability.body: Handles retries, partial fills, native balance approvals, and RPC failures so the agent doesn't have to.

tools.title: Tool
tools.intro: A single execution tool with flexible, composable parameters. The agent defines the order configuration, and Orbs handles the execution flow.

autoswap.body: Agent-driven token swaps with smart routing and slippage protection. The default for most trades.

autolimit.title: AUTOLIMIT
autolimit.body: Limit orders with on-chain execution guarantees. Set a price, walk away.

secureswap.title: SECURESWAP
secureswap.body: Additional cosigned oracle verification for higher-stakes trades. Extra checks before anything moves.

twap.title: TWAP
twap.body: Spread large trades over time to minimize price impact. Configurable duration and slicing.

oracle.title: Cosigned oracle verification
oracle.statement: Every execution is independently verified. No single agent, wallet, or operator can push a trade through without oracle cosignature.

steps.decide: Agent decides what to do based on its policy and market inputs.
steps.submit: Agent submits execution parameters via an Orbs Agentic tool.
steps.price: Orbs cosigned oracle provides signed input and output token prices. Smart contracts verify execution parameters and enforce slippage and price conditions to protect the user (agent).
steps.cosign: If the checks pass, the oracle cosigns the execution. The transaction is then verified and enforced on-chain by the smart contracts.

architecture.alt: An agent calling an Orbs Agentic tool, with the Orbs Network handling routing and cosigned-oracle verification before the trade settles on-chain.
